author: HiddenGap
text:
We've spent a considerable amount of time looking at the "What" we want to see. But we should not forget the importance of the "Where" we want to see it.

Take a look at this EUR/JPY 60 Min. Chart.

Let's look at the Confirmation Long signal first. This appears to be a nice example of the signal. However, there is a reason not to take this signal long. We have already established that we only need 1 pip/tick of one interval of the signal in or on a Supply/Demand Delta Zone for a long. Based on that, would we want to take a long trade if 1pip/tick of the signal is in or on a Supply/Demand Delta Zone? No. So this set-up would be disregarded because at least one pip of one interval is in the wrong place.

The Confirmation Short signal basically sets up entirely within a Supply/Demand Delta Zone. That does not mean price can't go down of course. It just means if it is going down, it's going down without us. As we prefer to take Longs in Demand and Shorts in Supply

author: akifusenet
text:
After all this discussion about WHAT we are looking for, I have been recently working on the WHERE part. The zones… And I believe this will make our purist RTM style friends happier because it is based on Flag Limit. I believe HG explained this better on a FF message but I cant find the reference for it. At least this is what I get with my limited intelligence and understanding: In this S/D world we can have 2 kind of zones. First is for touch trading and second is for waiting confirmation signals to happen in that zone. What HG is posting on this journal is the second type. WHERE is the Supply/Demand Delta Zones he identified and WHAT is the confirmation+entry signal/pattern. As far as I know he is not doing touch trading. But when you do touch trade, you don’t need the WHAT part of the equation. Zone itself become the signal/pattern. WHERE and WHAT are unified. I really liked the collaborative effort for fine tuning the Confirmation Entry so I believe we can construct a nice zone definition here.

The flag limit has a perfect definition here on RTM Markepedia and there are tons of examples of it. But I really like to have specific rules for it. So there will be no discussion if this is a valid zone or not. If it passes my rule set it is a valid zone if not it is not. So this is just one of the possible variations of a valid FL. Ok, I will stop mumbling and here is my definition as starting point. A picture is better than a thousand words so we will start with a picture.

Whats below is for bullish, reverse for bearish. We start with searching for 3 consecutive bars conforming 1. Candle 2 “OR” 3 is a WRB 2. Candle 1 “AND” 2 is White (Open<Close) 3. Candle 1 has a higher high than candle 2 4. Candle 2 has a higher high than candle 3 5. Candle 1 has a higher close than candle 2 6. Candle 2 has a higher close than candle 3

If these rules are passed we found our candidate consecutive bar chain. Now we are looking to the left to find some fractal highs.

Candle 2 and candle 3 are our candidates for closing higher than these fractal highs. We will check them separately. Candle 2 or candle3 must be the first candle reaching these fractal highs. (Meaning there shouldn’t be any candle which has a equal or higher high than the fractal high in between the fractal and the our candle 2/3.

Now the rules between fractal highs and our candle2 /candle3: 1. FH(meaning Fractal High) must be higher than Open of candle 2/3 2. FH must be lower than Close of candle 2/3 3. (For candle2) Open of candle2 must be lower than the low of candle1 4. (For candle3) Open of candle3 must be lower than the low of candle2 5. (For candle2) ZONE= High of candle2 and Low of candle1 6. (For candle3) ZONE= High of candle3 and Low of candle2 For now there isn’t any constraint for the number of FHs to be closed over. Only one FH is enough for a zone to be valid. Sorry this was a quick write up. I will edit later, hopefully in editing time window, to make it more understandable. HG, sorry for cluttering your journal. If you think this is unrelated please say so then I will stop posting  In the next post I will try to add some more charts. Pls give your suggestions for refinement, additions or different variations.

Akif,

author: akifusenet
text:
Ok one more refinement and after that some test results.

Additional rule: Always easier with a picture:

Our flag limit basically constructed from two candles. Lets call them c1(latest) and c2(prev). A supply zone is constructed from High of c1 and Low of c2. Lets call the candle previous of c2,-> c3. For a supply zone, Low of c3 should not go lower than High of c1 meaning Low of c3 should not poke into our zone. Reverse for demand zone.

Now test results.

After some initial refinements. I want to put it into a simple test. Test done on EURUSD H1 chart. (painfully by hand:) Starting from year 2015 onwards. Trading strategy is simple. -After the zone is validated put pending orders for 6 mini lots. -Zone borders are practically entry and stopLoss levels. -When your profit is equal to your risk(Entry-SL) ->RR1(RiskReward1) reached then close 3 positions(Now other 3 mini lots are free trades) -At each WRB over the RR1 level close 1 mini lot. Every WRB must give better reward than the previous one. I attached an excel file for the results for all the gory detailed numbers.

If you are too busy to look it. Here is the summary. It is not a holy grail. (Which is a good thing imo:) 56 trades done. 25 losers. 6 break evens. 25 winners. But good thing except 2 big losses, we managed to keep losses small and winners big. Average loss is 110 pip and average win is 240 pip. Btw no money management and risk management done for the sake of keeping things simple. Otherwise maybe we would not enter those 2 big loss trades with 6 mini lots because of high risk.(big zone)

Total gain after 56 trades 3258.39 pips.

author: HiddenGap
text:
There's nothing left to do with the CE, except define the rule set.

This started out as a collaboration, and will only continue as such. Therefore, the rules will only be given out as others post examples of the CE on their charts with explanations of the perceived specific rule, or entire rule-set.

I will start the ball rolling with what I believe is one of the most important rules.

The WRB

1) A valid CE MUST have a BreakOut WRB interval. a. A BreakOut WRB is defined as a WRB that closes higher or lower than the range of the previous three intervals. 2) For a valid long CE signal, the BreakOut WRB must be a dark interval (open>close). 3) For a valid short CE signal, the BreakOut WRB must be a white interval (open<close).

This is really our "start point" as there is no signal without the appearance of the WRB

(4) The long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than the lower shadows of all the intervals after the dark breakout WRB. (5) The long Lower Shadow of the DSS candle must be greater than both the lower shadows and the bodies of the 3 intervals Prior to the dark breakout WRB.
